answer:
RESULTS — Wealth inequality for white males and white females, 1990 → 1996 (nominal dollars; cross-sectional comparison of the same nominal sample; conventions exactly as agreed).

HEADLINE FIGURES (white males N=3,469; white females N=3,630; full tables in analysis/results_output.txt and analysis/REPORT.md)

White males: mean 88,163→131,792 (+49.5%); SD 244,717→317,464 (+29.7%); P50 15,601→8,900 (−43.0%); P75 91,400→148,055 (+62.0%); P90 215,149→333,640 (+55.1%); P99 1,325,291→1,789,903 (+35.1%); IQR 91,400→148,055 (+62.0%); P90−P50 +62.7%; P90/P50 13.79→37.49; share ≤0: 29.3%→45.2% (+15.9 pp); top-10% share of positive wealth 0.617→0.618 (+0.1 pp); top-1% share 0.229→0.182 (−4.7 pp); Gini(truncated-at-0) 0.780→0.793 (+1.3 pp).
White females: mean 99,605→128,837 (+29.3%); SD 264,818→299,693 (+13.2%); P50 20,100→8,825 (−56.1%); P75 109,000→152,875 (+40.3%); P90 242,550→331,750 (+36.8%); P99 1,015,687→1,789,755 (+76.2%); IQR +40.3%; P90−P50 +45.2%; P90/P50 12.07→37.59; share ≤0: 25.3%→44.5% (+19.2 pp); top-10% share 0.587→0.591 (+0.4 pp); top-1% share 0.217→0.178 (−3.9 pp); Gini(trunc) 0.761→0.777 (+1.6 pp).
P10=P25=0 in every year for both groups, so P75/P25 and P90/P10 are undefined in both years; proportional changes on non-positive bases are written "undefined".

CONCORDANT (six-plus measures, both sexes): SD up; P75, P90, P99 up strongly in dollars; IQR up 40–62%; P90−P50 up; P90/P50 roughly tripled; Gini(trunc) up 1.3–1.6 pp; share at-or-below-zero up 16–19 pp. Upper-half dispersion and bottom mass expansion moved together.

DISCORDANT: P50 fell while all upper percentiles rose; the top-1% share FELL 4–5 pp (concentration at the very top did not rise); and the positive-subsample Gini FELL 7–8 pp — among positive-wealth holders the distribution flattened, largely compositionally, as the 1996 positive subsample absorbs many low-wealth former zero/negative holders.

JAIL STRATA (descriptive only): White males ever_jailed=1 (N=57) had far lower levels (mean ~26k vs ~89k; P50 1,400→0), share ≤0 38.6%→56.1%, and higher Gini(trunc) (~0.86–0.87 vs ~0.78–0.79). White females ever_jailed=1 (N=12) is far too small for any inference; two-thirds or more at/below zero both years; figures reported with cell sizes but explicitly unstable.

DUPLICATE SENSITIVITY (flagged as requested): dropping exact full-row duplicates (648 male, 516 female rows, mostly zero/low-wealth ties) preserves the direction of every headline change (IQR up, P90−P50 up, Gini(trunc) up ~1.2–1.7 pp, top-10% share flat) but REVERSES or flattens the P50 change (deduplicated male P50 31,600→37,100 up; female 37,450→37,054 flat). The median decline is therefore an artefact of differential duplication of zero-wealth rows and is not leaned on.

HYPOTHESIS (final answer): Between 1990 and 1996 wealth inequality increased for both white males and white females in this NLSY79 sample, driven by upper-tail expansion rather than top concentration. For both groups the mean rose (+49.5% and +29.3%) while robust upper-half spreads widened sharply — SD, IQR, P90−P50, P75/P90/P99 levels, the P90/P50 ratio (from ~12–14 to ~37), and the zero-truncated Gini (+1.3–1.6 pp) all rose concordantly — accompanied by a 16–19 percentage-point growth in the share of the group at or below zero wealth. The pattern was similar for both sexes, though male gains at P75/P90 and the widening of the P90/P50 ratio were somewhat larger, while female gains were larger at P99. The increase is not visible at the median (whose apparent fall is a duplication artefact), the top-1% share of positive wealth actually declined slightly, and among positive-wealth holders the distribution flattened; the inequality rise is best characterised as a hollowing-out of the bottom (growing zero/negative mass) combined with strong nominal gains at the 75th percentile and above.

CAVEATS: nominal dollars (deflation would modestly shrink increases); no respondent ID, so 1990 and 1996 are cross-sections of the same nominal sample, not within-person changes; ever_jailed is a fixed 1985–1994 label and jail cells (57 and 12) cannot support inference; ratios with zero/negative bases reported as undefined; SD remains tail-sensitive, which is why the robust percentile measures carry the conclusion.

payload.workflow: Structural audit of data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows; no missing values) -> per-year, per-white-gender-group statistics in nominal dollars: mean, SD, percentiles P10-P99, IQR, P90-P50, P50-P10, P90/P50 ratio (undefined when base<=0), share at or below zero, top-10% and top-1% shares of aggregate positive wealth, Gini on full group truncated at zero (same convention both years) with positive-subsample Gini as sensitivity -> descriptive jail-status splits with cell sizes (N=57 and N=12, no inference) -> duplicate-row sensitivity check -> concordance/discordance synthesis.
